items.title: Diagonal Bianchi I model
items.statement:
Let $c>0$ be a fixed conversion constant in metres per second. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of physical time in seconds, and let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ have dimensionless angular coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3$. Its quotient charts are local lifts to $\mathbb R^3$; chart changes are translations by elements of $(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$. Give $M=I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the product smooth structure, so $M$ is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Here a **$C^2$ time-oriented Lorentzian metric datum** means a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ with $C^2$ components in smooth charts, whose value at each point has inertia $(3,1,0)$, together with a smooth vector field $N$ satisfying $g(N,N)<0$ everywhere. This is the explicit $C^2$ variant of the pointwise signature and time-orientation conditions in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; that supplier's metric regularity itself is smooth. Choose positive $C^2$ functions $a_i:I\to(0,\infty)$, $i=1,2,3$, with values in metres, and set

$$g=-c^2\,dt^2+\sum_{i=1}^3a_i(t)^2\,(dx^i)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_t.$$

In every lifted product chart, $g$ has matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-c^2,a_1^2,a_2^2,a_3^2)$, so it is symmetric, $C^2$, and has inertia $(3,1,0)$; $N$ is smooth and $g(N,N)=-c^2<0$. Thus $(M,g,N)$ is a $C^2$ time-oriented Lorentzian metric datum in the stated sense. This diagonal, spatially homogeneous metric datum is called a diagonal Bianchi I datum here; homogeneity means its coefficients are independent of the torus coordinates, and no isotropy is required. Define the directional expansion rates, their mean, the spatial volume scale and the squared directional shear by

$$H_i:=\frac{\dot a_i}{a_i},\qquad H:=\frac13\sum_{i=1}^3H_i,\qquad V:=a_1a_2a_3,\qquad \sigma^2:=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^3(H_i-H)^2.$$

Here $\dot a_i=d a_i/dt$; $H_i$ and $H$ have units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $V$ has units $\mathrm{m}^3$, and $\sigma^2$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-2}$. The symbol $\sigma^2$ denotes a nonnegative scalar defined by this formula, not a tensor norm on a spacetime frame. This is a geometric ansatz and makes no field-equation or observational claim. The product and quotient constructions carry the inherited axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use no stronger choice principle.

For comparison with smooth Lorentzian geometry, use the curvature convention $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ and the component order $R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$. The local connection and Ricci components for this $C^2$ metric are defined separately.

items.title: C2 curvature for the diagonal Bianchi I quotient metric
items.reference: prose-scaffold.md (FX10; added local C2 curvature definition)
items.statement:
For a diagonal Bianchi I datum, use local quotient coordinates $x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3$, with indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and let $(g_{ab})$ and $(g^{ab})$ be the displayed metric matrix and its inverse. At this $C^2$ regularity, define

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}:=\frac12g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

$$R^a{}_{bcd}:=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb}+\sum_{e=0}^3\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr),$$

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a=0}^3R^a{}_{bad},\qquad \mathcal R:=\sum_{b,d=0}^3g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12\mathcal R\,g_{ab},\qquad G^a{}_b:=\sum_{c=0}^3g^{ac}G_{cb}.$$

Repeated upper and lower indices in the first two displays are summed over $\{0,1,2,3\}$. The first formula gives coefficients symmetric in $b,c$ and, by expansion,

$$\Gamma^d{}_{ca}g_{db}+\Gamma^d{}_{cb}g_{ad}=\frac12(\partial_cg_{ab}+\partial_ag_{cb}-\partial_bg_{ca})+\frac12(\partial_cg_{ab}+\partial_bg_{ac}-\partial_ag_{cb})=\partial_cg_{ab}.$$

Thus these coefficients define a torsion-free, metric-compatible connection in every local quotient chart. It is unique: if $\Gamma'$ is another such connection, the lowered difference $C_{abc}:=g_{ad}(\Gamma'^d{}_{bc}-\Gamma^d{}_{bc})$ is symmetric in its last two indices by torsion freedom and skew in its first two by metric compatibility. Hence

$$C_{abc}=C_{acb}=-C_{cab}=-C_{cba}=C_{bca}=C_{bac}=-C_{abc},$$

so $C=0$. The curvature sign and index order agree with the smooth convention cited in the references below. Since $g$ is $C^2$, the coefficients $\Gamma$ are $C^1$ and the curvature and Ricci components are continuous. On overlaps, two local lifts differ by a constant translation: the Jacobian is the identity and all second derivatives of the transition map vanish. The metric arrays and their derivatives therefore agree, so the displayed connection and curvature arrays patch consistently over the quotient atlas. This is a local $C^2$ extension for this fixed atlas; no general low-regularity tensoriality theorem is being assumed. It inherits only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from the torus and product definitions.

items.title: Curvature components of the diagonal Bianchi I metric
items.reference: prose-scaffold.md (FX10; added local curvature component lemma)
items.statement:
For a diagonal Bianchi I datum, write $H_\Sigma:=H_1+H_2+H_3=3H$. In every local quotient chart, the only nonzero Christoffel symbols are $\Gamma^0{}_{ii}=a_i^2H_i/c^2$ and $\Gamma^i{}_{0i}=\Gamma^i{}_{i0}=H_i$. The possibly nonzero lowered curvature components are exactly those obtained from the following values by the displayed sign reversals:

$$R_{0i0i}=R_{i0i0}=-a_i^2(\dot H_i+H_i^2),\qquad R_{0ii0}=R_{i00i}=a_i^2(\dot H_i+H_i^2),$$

$$R_{ijij}=R_{jiji}=\frac{a_i^2a_j^2}{c^2}H_iH_j,\qquad R_{ijji}=R_{jiij}=-\frac{a_i^2a_j^2}{c^2}H_iH_j\quad(1\le i<j\le3).$$

The Ricci components are

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=-\sum_{i=1}^3(\dot H_i+H_i^2),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ii}=\frac{a_i^2}{c^2}(\dot H_i+H_iH_\Sigma),$$

and every off-diagonal Ricci component is zero.

items.title: Kasner vacuum constraints
items.statement: Let $a_i(t)=A_i(t/t_0)^{p_i}$ on a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq(0,\infty)$, where $A_i>0$ are lengths in metres, $t_0>0$ is a time in seconds, and $p_i\in\mathbb R$ are dimensionless exponents. These $p_i$ are called Kasner exponents for this power-law branch; define their sums $P:=\sum_{i=1}^3p_i$ and $Q:=\sum_{i=1}^3p_i^2$. For a nonstatic datum, meaning that not all $p_i$ vanish, the geometric vacuum equation $\operatorname{Ric}=0$ in the $C^2$ curvature definition of this page holds exactly when $P=Q=1$. If all $p_i=0$, then the full curvature tensor vanishes, so the metric is flat in the curvature sense. These are exact statements about the specified finite-dimensional metrics; no singularity or generic cosmological conclusion follows.

references.title: Rishabh Jha, Introduction to Hamiltonian Formulation of General Relativity and Homogeneous Cosmologies, SciPost Physics Lecture Notes 73 (2023), arXiv:2204.03537v2, Section 4.3.1, equations (159)–(172), printed pp. 36–38 (PDF pp. 37–39)

items.title: Diagonal-source shear equation and isotropic-source decay
items.statement:
For a diagonal Bianchi I datum, let $\Lambda$ be a constant in $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ and let $Q_i:I\to\mathbb R$ be continuous functions in $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. Suppose the spatial diagonal equations

$$G^i{}_i+\Lambda=Q_i(t)\qquad(i=1,2,3;\ \text{no sum over }i)$$

hold, where $G^i{}_i$ is defined by the local $C^2$ curvature convention on this page. With $\Delta_{ij}:=H_i-H_j$ and $H_\Sigma:=3H$, subtracting the equations gives

$$\dot\Delta_{ij}+3H\Delta_{ij}=c^2\bigl(Q_i-Q_j\bigr).$$

If the diagonal source is isotropic, meaning $Q_1=Q_2=Q_3$, then $V\Delta_{ij}$ is constant for each pair, and there is a constant $C\ge0$ with units $\mathrm{m}^6\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ such that $\sigma^2=C\,V^{-2}$ throughout $I$. For unequal diagonal sources the right-hand side remains; this proposition makes no unsourced $V^{-2}$ claim in that case.

references.title: Diego L. Cáceres, Leonardo Castañeda, and Juan M. Tejeiro, Shear Dynamics in Bianchi I Cosmology, arXiv:1003.3491v1 (2010), Section 2, equations (2.1)–(2.2), and Section 2.1, equations (1.6), (2.8)–(2.17), printed pp. 2–4 (PDF pp. 3–5)

title: Cosmological dynamics and anisotropic shear — Examples

items.title: Nonflat anisotropic Kasner exponents
items.statement: On any nonempty open interval $I\subseteq(0,\infty)$, the exponents $(p_1,p_2,p_3)=(-1/3,2/3,2/3)$ with $a_i=A_i(t/t_0)^{p_i}$, $A_i>0$ lengths in metres and $t_0>0$ a time in seconds, give a nonstatic Ricci-flat diagonal Bianchi I metric. Its directional expansion rates are unequal, the scalar $\sigma^2:=\frac12\sum_i(H_i-H)^2$ equals $1/(3t^2)$, and its curvature component $R_{0101}=-4a_1^2/(9t^2)$ is nonzero. Thus the Riemann tensor is nonzero and the metric is not flat.

references.title: Rishabh Jha, Introduction to Hamiltonian Formulation of General Relativity and Homogeneous Cosmologies, SciPost Physics Lecture Notes 73 (2023), arXiv:2204.03537v2, Section 4.3.1, equations (159)–(172), printed pp. 36–38 (PDF pp. 37–39)

items.title: A locally flat Kasner coordinate branch
items.statement:
For lengths $A_i>0$ in metres and a time $t_0>0$ in seconds, set $I=(0,\infty)$ and take the exponents $(p_1,p_2,p_3)=(1,0,0)$, so $a_1=A_1(t/t_0)$ and $a_2=A_2$, $a_3=A_3$. They satisfy $\sum_i p_i=1$ and $\sum_i p_i^2=1$, and the corresponding diagonal Bianchi I metric is Ricci-flat with identically zero Riemann tensor on $I$. Define the open coordinate domain $\mathcal D:=\{(T,X,z_2,z_3)\in\mathbb R^4:T>|X|\}$ and its Minkowski metric $\eta:=-dT^2+dX^2+dz_2^2+dz_3^2$, with all four coordinates measured in metres. In any local quotient chart with lifted dimensionless angular coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3$, let $\alpha:=A_1/(ct_0)$ and define

$$\Phi(t,x^1,x^2,x^3):=(ct\cosh(\alpha x^1),\;ct\sinh(\alpha x^1),\;A_2x^2,\;A_3x^3).$$

This map is a local isometry from the chart domain, with the Bianchi I metric, onto an open subset of $(\mathcal D,\eta)$. Its scale factor $a_1$ tends to zero as $t\downarrow0$, but that excluded coordinate boundary alone does not establish curvature blowup or a global extension on the torus quotient.
